title: DOM XSS on duckduckgo.com search

scenario.summary: DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) reported against DuckDuckGo.
preconditions: Client-side JavaScript reads attacker-influenceable data (location, referrer, postMessage, localStorage) and writes it into the DOM via a dangerous sink

process.action: Enumerate client-side sources (location.hash, location.search, document.referrer, postMessage handlers)
process.expected_observation: List of sources the app reads on page load or event

process.action: Trace source values to dangerous sinks (innerHTML, document.write, eval, setAttribute)
process.expected_observation: A source flows unsanitized into a sink

process.action: Craft a payload for the specific source (e.g. URL fragment) matching the sink's execution context
process.expected_observation: Payload executes purely client-side, no server round-trip needed

process.action: Confirm the payload survives routing/SPA framework processing (React/Vue/Angular escaping)
process.expected_observation: Execution occurs despite framework's default escaping, e.g. via dangerouslySetInnerHTML equivalents

impact: Client-side-only compromise that can bypass server-side WAFs entirely
Session/token theft, UI redress, or malicious in-page actions
remediation: Avoid dangerous DOM sinks; use textContent/safe framework bindings instead of innerHTML
Sanitize any source-derived value before it reaches a sink, even client-side
Adopt Trusted Types where supported by the browser target
